author: ribeye
dek: Milwaukee rallied from 4-0 down to stun the two-time defending champions — and a Lancaster family stayed up way past bedtime to watch it happen.
disclaimer: Parody: the Keller family of Lancaster is fictional. The Brewers sweeping the Dodgers is real, as reported by the Associated Press in October 2026.
headline: Brewers Sweep Dodgers to Reach First World Series Since 1982, and One Lancaster Living Room May Never Recover

ohio_story: LANCASTER, Ohio — Mark Keller did everything right. He set the DVR, he put the kids to bed at a reasonable hour, he told his wife, Jen, that he would watch "just the first couple of innings" of Game 4 and be asleep by ten. Then Shohei Ohtani hit a three-run homer in the second, the Dodgers went up 4-0, and Keller — a Brewers fan by marriage, his wife having grown up outside Milwaukee — found himself standing in his socks in the middle of his Lancaster living room at midnight, whispering "chip away, chip away" at a television that could not hear him.

"I have sat through Ohio State-Michigan games in a blizzard, I have sat through a Lancaster Golden Gales rain delay that lasted longer than the game, but I have never whispered at a baseball team from Fairfield County at 12:30 in the morning," Keller said, eating cold Skyline chili straight from the container the next morning. "When Mitchell hit that ball in the sixth, I yelled so loud the dog hid under the porch. Jen came downstairs and just stood there in her robe like, 'Oh, so we're doing this now.'" By the ninth, both kids were awake on the couch in their pajamas, Jen had made a second pot of coffee, and the whole family was chanting along with the Brewers fans at Dodger Stadium.

The Kellers are now facing the consequences. Mark has promised his father-in-law in Wisconsin that the whole family will drive up for a World Series game — a plan Jen describes as "eight hours in the minivan, which honestly sounds relaxing compared to last night" — and his son, Eli, 11, has already informed his teacher that he will be "emotionally unavailable" until Oct. 23. The family dog, Biscuit, has still not come out from under the porch. Back in Lancaster, a neighbor has offered to mow their lawn while they're gone, on one condition: if the Brewers win it all, the Kellers have to bring back a pennant for his garage.
real_summary: After 44 years, the Milwaukee Brewers are going back to the World Series. Propelled by a lockdown bullpen and repeated comebacks, the young Brewers swept the two-time defending champion Los Angeles Dodgers out of the playoffs on Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026, with a 6-4 victory in Game 4 of the National League Championship Series at Dodger Stadium.

Shohei Ohtani's first home run of the postseason — a three-run shot in the second inning — helped put the Dodgers ahead 4-0 before Milwaukee chipped away. Garrett Mitchell hit a go-ahead homer in the sixth inning, David Hamilton added a two-out solo shot in the ninth, and Aaron Ashby pitched three scoreless innings for the save as the Brewers won their first National League pennant. Milwaukee, which topped the majors with 103 wins during the regular season, will host the World Series opener on Oct. 23 against Cleveland or Tampa Bay. First baseman Jake Bauers was named NLCS MVP.

The sweep made history twice over. Milwaukee became the first major league club to finish a postseason sweep after getting swept by that same opponent in the previous postseason — Los Angeles had taken all four NLCS games against the Brewers last season — and the first team to sweep a best-of-seven postseason series in which it trailed in every game. The Brewers' only previous World Series appearance came in 1982, when they were still in the American League and lost in seven games to the St. Louis Cardinals. They have never won a World Series.
source_note: AP reporting, Oct 2026: Brewers sweep Dodgers 6-4 in Game 4 of the NLCS on Oct. 15 to reach the World Series for the first time since 1982.
